name: Zifuli
description: Zifuli is a 5-player variant of Cöch (Cucco), an Italian partnership trick-taking game from Bergamo. Uses the special 40-card Cucco deck (20 pairs). 8 cards each. Bidding phase determines secret partnerships: bid by naming a card you hold, the holder of the other copy becomes your partner (hidden until card is played). Can bid both copies = play alone. Overcall only by lower card of same suit. Win by capturing more card points (19 total).

history.origins: 5-player variant of Cöch/Cucco from Bergamo, Italy. Described by Anthony Smith in The Playing-Card Vol XX No 1 (1991).
history.cultural: Regional Italian card game tradition from Bergamo.
history.evolution: Variant of the traditional Cucco game played near Lake Iseo.

setup.deck: 40-card Cucco deck: 20 pairs. Figure suit (I-X, Roman numerals) + Matte suit (Matto, Mascherone, Secchia, Nulla, XI Osteria, XII Gatto, XIII Cavallo, XIIII Bragon, XV Cucco, Brescia). In Zifuli: Matto ranks between Nulla and Osteria (not lowest).

rules.objective: Win tricks containing valuable cards. Side with 10+ of 19 points wins.
rules.gameplay: Bidding: name a card you hold; holder of matching copy = secret partner. Overcall with lower card of same suit only. Can call card you hold both copies of = play alone. Play: no trumps, follow suit, highest of led suit wins, first of equal cards beats second. Card points: Figure V-VIIII=½pt, X=1pt; Matte XI-XV+Brescia=1pt each. Total 19pts.

scoring.description: Bidder's side wins: opponents each pay 1 stake (bidder gets 2, partner gets 1). Bidder loses: reversed. Solo bidder wins: 8 stakes (2 from each); loses: pays 2 to each.
scoring.winCondition: Win tricks containing valuable cards. Side with 10+ of 19 points wins.
